  "evidence": "The example has `rule: WR-008` and `fix_safety: safe`. Its evidence only says “configuration file” and “environment variable,” but the suggested action invents `/etc/app/config.yaml`, `DB_HOST`, and “database hostname.” WR-008 defaults to `review-required`, and no controlling repository policy supplies those exact details.",
  "impact": "This canonical example teaches reviewers to auto-apply an illegal upgrade and invent operational identifiers and paths, which can produce technically wrong procedures.",

description:

  "line": "81, 141-145",
  "evidence": "The `safe` examples include applying consistent terminology and correcting a factually wrong date/version. WR-001 defaults to `review-required`; WR-012 defaults to `report-only`; `fix-safety.md:87` prohibits upgrades; `fix-safety.md:166` itself says an inaccurate protected date is report-only; and `fix-safety.md:202-210` prohibits automatic changes to necessary provenance regardless of classification.",
  "impact": "A consumer can treat a canonical-term choice or historical date/version edit as automatically applicable, silently changing meaning or provenance despite the central safety contract.",
  "fix": "Remove these examples from `safe`. State that `safe` is reachable only when explicit repository policy supplies the exact replacement and all invariants hold. Never use dates, versions, tickets, authorship, URLs, identifiers, commands, literals, quoted text, or other prohibited content as `safe` examples."
}
